title: Decide whether task edit --status <terminal> should relocate the record like task complete does
description: Surfaced by opum-agent (2026-09-03) while reviewing QCLI-220 (the task view/list path field): task complete relocates a record into .quest/completed/ (tasks.ts complete() calls moveTask(reference, "completed", ...)), but task edit --status <terminal-status> (and its transition() alias) never does -- editOn() (tasks.ts ~812-876) always writes in place via this.repository.write(...), regardless of whether the new status is terminal. Verified directly in this repository, not relayed. Cross-repo evidence the orchestrator supplied and I have not independently re-verified: in lore-cli, LCLI-429 (closed via task complete) sits in .quest/completed/ while LCLI-430 (closed via task edit --status Done) sits in .quest/tasks/; in opum-agent, all 25 Done tasks remain under .quest/tasks/ because that session only ever uses task edit. Net effect: two tasks sharing the same terminal status can legitimately live in different directories depending on which command closed them. This does not affect QCLI-220s path field, which reads the records real on-disk location rather than deriving it from status -- but it is a real, independent question about whether the location move is part of quest's intended lifecycle contract or an artifact of edit and complete having grown different side effects.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision is recorded: either (a) reaching a terminal status through task edit/transition is defined to also relocate the record the same way task complete does, or (b) the two are intentionally different (edit as a plain field patch vs. complete as a lifecycle ceremony with retention) and that distinction is documented where a consumer would look for it

If (a): editOn detects a transition into a terminal status and performs the same relocation moveTask(complete) does, with a migration note for existing repositories that already have terminal-status tasks sitting in .quest/tasks/
If (b): the tracker overview or task-execution guide documents that status alone does not imply location, and that only task complete/archive/demote move a record on disk
Either way, quest doctor is checked for whether it already flags (or should flag) a terminal-status task outside .quest/completed/ as a consistency issue

implementationNotes:
Decided: (b) -- intentionally different. task complete/archive/demote are lifecycle ceremony WITH retention (they move the file); task edit --status <terminal> (and its transition() alias) is a plain field patch and does NOT relocate, staying wherever the record already was. Two tasks sharing the same terminal status legitimately live in different storage locations depending on which command reached it -- this is by design, not an artifact.

Why (b) over (a): archive() already fully decouples status from location today -- an archived task can carry ANY status (per this repo's own documented model, "an archived task stays readable" regardless of what state it was in when archived), so "status implies location" was already false before this task existed. Auto-relocating only on edit-into-Done (option a) would have created an inconsistent special case -- one status/command pairing magically moving the file while every other combination (archived-with-any-status, demoted, or edited into any non-terminal status) does not -- without fixing the actual generalization. QCLI-219 (landed just before this task) also makes the operational stakes here much lower than when this was filed: view/list/edit now all resolve a task by id across every location correctly regardless of where it physically sits, so a Done task in the "wrong" directory no longer breaks anything functionally -- it's purely a storage-layout question, and Quest's own storage layout is explicitly not something callers are meant to interact with directly ("do not edit .quest/ by hand, drive it through quest").

AC3: documented in the workspace-setup guide (agents/guides.ts) -- "Status and on-disk location are deliberately independent... only task complete/archive/demote relocate a record... every command that reads a task resolves it by id across every location regardless" -- and as a doc comment directly on TaskService.transition() so a future reader of the source sees the same reasoning at the point they might otherwise "fix" this as an oversight.

AC4: checked quest doctor's actual implementation (PlanningService.doctor, src/application/planning/planning.ts) -- its only current check is milestone_task_not_found (a milestone referencing a nonexistent task id). It has no location/status consistency check at all today, and per decision (b) it should NOT gain one: flagging a Done-task-outside-completed/ as an "issue" would be a false positive against the now-decided-intentional behavior (and would also flag every pre-cutover migrated task that never went through complete(), a large and legitimate population in this repo alone). No doctor change made; the absence is now a documented decision, not an unexamined gap.

Pinned with a regression test (test/integration/tasks/cli-semantics.test.ts) rather than left as prose alone: a task reaching Done through edit stays in tasks/; a task reaching Done through complete relocates to completed/; both resolve identically via task view regardless. Full suite 422/422, bun run check green.
finalSummary:
Decided: status and on-disk location are intentionally independent. task complete/archive/demote are lifecycle ceremony with retention (they physically relocate the record); task edit --status <terminal> is a plain field patch and does not relocate, staying wherever the record already was. Two tasks sharing the same terminal status can legitimately live in different storage directories depending on which command reached it.

Chosen over auto-relocating edit --status into completed/ because archive() already fully decouples status from location today (an archived task legitimately carries any status), so 'status implies location' was already false; adding a special case only for edit-into-Done would have been inconsistent rather than a real fix. QCLI-219 (landed immediately before this task) also removed the operational stakes: view/list/edit now resolve a task by id across every location correctly, so which physical directory a Done task sits in no longer affects functionality.

Documented in the workspace-setup guide and as a doc comment on TaskService.transition(). quest doctor checked directly: its only existing check is milestone_task_not_found, with no location/status consistency check -- correctly so, since flagging this would be a false positive against the now-decided-intentional behavior and against this repo's own population of pre-cutover migrated tasks. Pinned with a regression test rather than left as prose alone. Full suite 422/422.
